query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of lattice distortions through high-pressure torsion (HPT) processing can increase the coercive field in magnetic high-entropy alloys by pinning domain walls, thus hindering magnetization reversal.
generation.material_initial_state: Magnetic high-entropy alloy in its as-cast state
generation.intervention: High-pressure torsion (HPT) processing at 5 GPa for 10 turns
generation.conditions: Room temperature, applied magnetic field not exceeding 10 Tesla
generation.mechanism: Pinning of domain walls by lattice defects, increasing the energy barrier for magnetization reversal
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in coercive field relative to the as-cast baseline
generation.baseline: As-cast magnetic high-entropy alloy without HPT processing
generation.boundary: Coercive field increase is expected to saturate at HPT pressures above 7 GPa
generation.uncertainty: The actual increase in coercive field may vary depending on the specific composition of the high-entropy alloy and the degree of lattice distortion achieved through HPT

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the coercive field of HPT-processed and as-cast samples using a vibrating sample magnetometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the HPT-processed sample is not at least 10% higher than that of the as-cast sample, the hypothesis is falsified
